To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the physiological characterization of 22 knockouts in central carbon metabolism reveals a complex and diverse set of responses; (2) the physiological data is not consistent with predictions from FBA; (3) MOMA and RELASH are able to predict the knockout data to a certain degree; and (4) the physiological data suggests that the knockout data cannot be predicted solely from the knockout of a single enzyme.
the knockouts have a wide range of effects on E. coli physiology and metabolism, which are difficult to predict with constraint-based models.

1) the physiological response of E. coli to gene knockouts is highly specific, and 2) the physiological response is significantly affected by kinetic effects and regulatory effects that are not captured by current constraint-based modeling approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic study of the physiological responses of E. coli to genetic perturbations.
the development and application of a novel, systematic approach that can be used to gain a deeper understanding of the physiology and metabolic capabilities of E. coli.
the development of methods and tools for the systematic characterization of the physiological impact of gene knock-outs in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gene knockouts have a significant impact on the physiology of E. coli.

the data presented here are a rich source of information that can be used to further develop our understanding of E. coli metabolism, and that the data-to-model comparisons provide important insights into how the models can be improved.
the data presented here is an important contribution to the field of systems biology and metabolic modeling, and that it provides a rich data set for further analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data reveal the complexity of cellular physiology, while the models provide a framework to understand the underlying principles.
the physiological data are consistent with the model predictions but that the data provide additional insights into E. coli physiology.

the physiological characterization of gene knockouts in E. coli central carbon metabolism provides an excellent resource for the scientific community, and the data analysis methods we have applied provide a framework for understanding how to interpret and integrate data from different omics technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of experimental measurements and constraint-based modeling can be used to understand the physiological consequences of gene knockouts, and that such an approach can reveal new insights into cellular physiology.
the physiological responses to gene knockouts are highly complex and context dependent, and thus require detailed experimental characterization.

a comprehensive, quantitative physiological characterization of knockout strains is essential to understand the complex interactions between the different parts of the metabolism and to develop predictive metabolic models.
